CausalChain: Chitosan nanoparticles conjugated with hepatocyte-targeting ligands -> Targeted delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 to HCC cells -> Survivin knockout leads to increased apoptosis and tumor antigen release -> Enhanced dendritic cell activation and T-cell priming -> Improved response to immune checkpoint inhibitors -> Synergistic anti-tumor response in HCC
Hypothesis: Targeted CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of survivin in HCC cells using ligand-conjugated biodegradable chitosan nanoparticles will induce apoptosis and boost tumor immunogenicity, thereby synergizing with immune checkpoint blockade to enhance anti-tumor responses in hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: We propose a novel combination strategy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) therapy, in which targeted CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated disruption of the anti‐apoptotic gene survivin, delivered using ligand‐conjugated biodegradable chitosan nanoparticles, synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade. The nanoparticle platform can be engineered to target hepatocytes via specific ligands such as galactose or AFP promoter elements, thereby ensuring selective delivery of the gene editing system. Survivor knockout in HCC cells is expected to induce apoptotic cell death and release tumor antigens that promote dendritic cell activation and effector T‐cell recruitment. In turn, this cascade may potentiate the efficacy of checkpoint inhibitors that reverse T‐cell exhaustion, ultimately leading to enhanced tumor control and improved patient outcomes.
